title: Judges 19
paragraphs: ¹ In those days, when there was no king in Israel, a Levite living in a remote part of the hill country of Ephraim took a woman from Bethlehem in Judah as his concubine. ² But she was unfaithful to him and left, returning to her father's house in Bethlehem, where she stayed for four months. ³ Her husband set out after her to speak tenderly to her and bring her back. He had his servant and a pair of donkeys with him. She brought him into her father's house, and when her father saw him, he was glad to meet him. ⁴ His father-in-law, the young woman's father, urged him to stay; so he remained there three days, and they ate and drank and spent the nights together. ⁵ On the fourth day they rose early to leave, but the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Have something to eat first, then you can be on your way."

⁶ So the two of them sat down and ate and drank together. Then the young woman's father said, "Please stay tonight and enjoy yourself." ⁷ When the man got up to leave, his father-in-law pressed him, so he spent another night there. ⁸ On the fifth day he rose early to go, but the young woman's father said, "Please refresh yourself first." They lingered until afternoon, and the two of them ate together. ⁹ When the man finally got up to leave with his concubine and servant, his father-in-law said, "Look, it's nearly evening — the day is almost gone. Stay the night. It'll be good for you, and tomorrow you can get an early start and head home." ¹⁰ But this time the man would not stay. He set out and traveled as far as Jebus — that is, Jerusalem — with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.

¹¹ When they were near Jebus, the day was almost gone, and the servant said to his master, "Let's stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here." ¹² His master replied, "We won't turn in to a foreign city where the people are not Israelites. We'll go on to Gibeah." ¹³ He told his servant, "Come, let's try to reach Gibeah or Ramah and spend the night in one of those places." ¹⁴ They pressed on, and the sun went down just as they were approaching Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin. ¹⁵ They turned off there to spend the night in Gibeah. The man went in and sat down in the town square, but no one took them in for the night.

¹⁶ That evening an old man came in from his work in the fields. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was living in Gibeah, though the townspeople were Benjamites. ¹⁷ He looked up and saw the traveler in the town square and asked, "Where are you going? Where did you come from?" ¹⁸ The man answered, "We're traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to a place in the hill country of Ephraim — that's where I'm from. I went to Bethlehem, and now I'm heading back home. But no one here has taken us in. ¹⁹ We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and the woman and our young servant. We don't need anything." ²⁰ "You are welcome," the old man said. "Let me provide everything you need. Just don't spend the night in the square."

²¹ He brought them into his house and fed the donkeys. They washed their feet and ate and drank. ²² While they were enjoying themselves, a mob of troublemakers from the town surrounded the house, pounding on the door. They shouted to the old man, the owner of the house, "Bring out the man who came to your house! We want to have sex with him." ²³ The owner of the house went outside and said to them, "No, my friends, please don't do such a wicked thing. This man is a guest in my house — don't commit this outrage. ²⁴ Look, here is my virgin daughter, and the man's concubine. Let me bring them out. You can have your way with them and do to them whatever you like. But don't do this disgraceful thing to this man." ²⁵ The men wouldn't listen. So the man took his concubine and pushed her outside to them. They raped her and abused her throughout the night until morning. When dawn broke, they let her go.

²⁶ At daybreak the woman came and collapsed at the doorway of the house where her master was staying and lay there until it grew light. ²⁷ When her master got up in the morning and opened the door to continue his journey, he found his concubine lying at the entrance with her hands on the threshold. ²⁸ "Get up," he said. "Let's go." But there was no answer. He lifted her onto the donkey and set out for home. ²⁹ When he reached his house, he took a knife and cut his concubine limb from limb into twelve pieces, then sent them throughout all the territories of Israel. ³⁰ Everyone who saw it declared, "Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen since the day the Israelites came up from Egypt. Think about it! What are we going to do? Let's hear what you have to say."
